farm.title: Your whole farm
farm.sub: All your fields together: what the farm could earn in a typical year and in a bad one, how your fields balance each other, and a plan that suits the whole farm. Each field uses the same numbers as its money page.
farm.support: This supports your own planning and your adviser. It does not replace them.
farm.switch_label: Look at one field or the whole farm
farm.add_help: Add this field to your whole farm, to plan it together with your other fields
farm.added_toast: {{name}} is in your farm ({{n}} fields). Open Whole farm to see them together.
farm.full: Your farm has the most fields this version can work out ({{n}}).
farm.find_field: Find a field on the map
farm.empty_h: Add fields: open a field and press Add to my farm
farm.empty: Most farms have several fields. Add yours one by one (Compare options, Make a plan and My fields each have an Add to my farm button) and see them here together.
farm.sample_help: Three real cropland fields in central Iowa (Story, Boone and Hamilton counties), from public field boundaries and USDA crop maps. The first time can take a few minutes while the fields are worked out.
farm.sample_failed: These sample fields could not be added just now: {{list}}. Try again later.
farm.loading_n: Working out {{n}} of {{m}} fields. The totals below cover the fields that are ready and update when the rest are done. A field nobody has opened before can take a few minutes.
farm.none_ready_title: No field can be worked out yet
farm.none_ready: None of these fields has money results yet.

left.no_money: money results are not available here
left.no_acres: no field size: type the acres
left.no_years: no weather years shared with the other fields
left.incomplete: needs your yield, price or costs on its money page

farm.k_fields_keep: all keep what they grow now

loss.none: No simulated year lost money for the whole farm.
loss.most: Almost every year, with these numbers.

farm.k_div_sub: how much better the farm's bad year is than its fields' bad years added up
farm.k_div_one: add a second field to see it
farm.fields_help: Change a plan or the acres and everything updates.
farm.acres_boundary: From the field boundary. Type your own if you know it better (the money page uses the same number).
farm.acres_yours: Your number (the money page uses the same number)
farm.lock_help: A locked field keeps its plan when you search for the best plan
farm.st_error: Could not be worked out just now.
farm.total_note: Farm totals are worked out year by year, so they are not the sum of the column.
farm.fields_foot: Typical and bad year are whole-field dollars a year, rounded to $100, with each field's own numbers from its money page.
farm.range_help: Each bar runs from the bad year (1 in 10) to the good year (1 in 10), whole farm dollars a year; the dot is the typical year. {{n}} simulated years each.
farm.range_cur: Every field keeps what it grows now
farm.range_aria: Bad year {{bad}}, typical {{typ}}, good year {{good}}, whole farm a year
farm.div_one: With one field, the farm's bad year is that field's bad year. Add another field to see how they balance each other.
farm.div_text: Because your fields don't all have their bad year at the same time, your farm's bad year is {{v}} better than adding up each field's bad year.
farm.div_none: Your fields tend to have their bad years at the same time, so the farm's bad year is about the same as adding up each field's bad year. Different crops in the same year spread the risk more.
farm.div_sum: Each field's bad year, added up
farm.div_corr: How closely the fields' yearly results move together: {{r}} on average (1 = always together, 0 = unrelated).
farm.div_weather: Fields within about 50 km share the same NASA POWER weather cell, so the model gives them the same weather; real fields differ more than that. Prices are the same for every field.

opt.h: Find the best plan for my farm
opt.help: Tries the options of every field together and keeps the plan that suits the whole farm best, within your limits. Locked fields keep their plan.
opt.goal_help_money: Most money: the highest typical year for the whole farm.
opt.goal_help_balanced: Balanced: the best mix of a good typical year and a good bad year.
opt.goal_help_safe: Safest: the best bad year (1 in 10) for the whole farm.
opt.goal_money: Goal: highest typical year for the farm
opt.goal_balanced: Goal: best average of the typical and the bad year
opt.goal_safe: Goal: best bad year for the farm
opt.cap: Most of the farm one crop may take
opt.live: Updated as you change your fields or settings.
opt.same: Your plan is already the best one found
opt.same_help: No other combination of your fields' options did better for the whole farm with these settings.
opt.beat: In past weather and prices, this plan would have beaten your plan as it stands in {{k}} years out of 10.
opt.cap_missed: No plan meets the crop limit with these fields' options; this is the closest one.
opt.r_change: From {{from}} to {{to}}. On its own this change adds {{typ}} to the farm's typical year and {{bad}} to its bad year.
opt.r_keep: Keeps {{name}}: nothing else did better for the farm.
opt.applied: The suggested plan is now your plan.
opt.caveats: Assumes each field is managed as it is now, uses regional weather (≈50 km) and USDA regional prices and costs unless you changed them on a field's money page. In past weather and prices this plan would have done this; it is not a promise.
opt.model: Whole-farm plan search on the FarmSmart crop simulation
opt.d_cap: Limit: one crop at most {{pct}} % of the farm in any year
opt.d_search: Deterministic search: field by field, every option, {{n}} sweeps
opt.conf_samples: Based on {{s}} real weather seasons ({{y0}}–{{y1}} starts) × {{p}} price years
opt.conf_few: Few seasons shared by all fields
opt.conf_no_prices: No price history: one price level only
opt.conf_beat: Beats your plan as it stands in {{k}} of 10 sampled years
opt.conf_usda: Most acres use USDA regional prices and costs, not your farm's
opt.conf_own: {{pct}} % of the acres use your own yields, prices or costs
opt.conf_regional: Regional weather (≈50 km), not an on-farm station
opt.caveat_mgmt: Same management assumed on every field
opt.raise: Type your own yields, prices and costs on each field's money page.
opt.r_cap: It is needed to keep every year within your crop limit.

farm.mix_help: Acres of each crop in years 1–5 of your plan. Year 1 follows each field's last crop on record.
farm.mix_foot: Spreading crops across fields in the same year spreads weather and price risk, and spreads the work.
farm.cash_help: A typical year for each of the next five years, whole farm: your plan vs every field keeping what it grows now. One-time switch costs from the money pages are paid in year 1.
farm.cash_help_keep: A typical year for each of the next five years, whole farm, with every field keeping what it grows now.
farm.cash_none: The year-by-year cash flow could not be worked out for every field.
farm.soil_help: Acre-weighted over the whole farm, for your plan.
farm.soil_partial: Covers {{a}} of {{b}} acres (the rest are still loading or have no soil results).
farm.soil_model: FarmSmart crop and soil simulation (compare cards, middle value)
farm.soil_d1: Each field's simulated rotation over its real weather years
farm.soil_r1: Simulated, not measured on your fields
farm.soil_r2: Soil carbon changes slowly; a trend takes many years to show
farm.soil_foot: Water use includes rain; more is not always worse. Soil carbon gains are slow and take years.
farm.n_method: Every field runs through the same {{s}} real weather seasons ({{y0}}–{{y1}} starts) × {{p}} USDA price years ({{p0}}–{{p1}}) = {{n}} simulated years per plan.
farm.n_method_noprice: Every field runs through the same {{s}} real weather seasons ({{y0}}–{{y1}} starts), with one price level.
farm.n_drought: Driest years: the farm's driest fifth of seasons (acre-weighted season rain at or below {{mm}} mm).
farm.n_align: Fields are lined up by year: a dry year or a low price year hits every field at once, as it would on a real farm.
farm.n_bad: Typical is the middle year of the farm; bad and good are the 1-in-10 low and high of the farm's rotation average.
farm.n_years: Chance of a losing year counts single years in which the whole farm lost money.
farm.n_same_inputs: Each field uses its own yields, prices, costs and settings from its money page; untouched fields use USDA regional averages.
farm.n_never: In past weather and prices a plan would have done this. Past patterns do not prove a switch will pay.
farm.si_model: FarmSmart crop simulation + money arithmetic, whole farm
farm.si_d_costs: USDA ERS operating costs, or your own
farm.si_r_regional: Regional weather (≈50 km), not measured on your fields
farm.si_r_own: {{n}} of {{m}} fields use some of your own numbers
farm.si_r_usda: USDA regional prices and costs, not your farm's
farm.si_raise: Type your own yields, prices and costs on each field's money page.
farm.demo_farm_hint: Three real fields in central Iowa, put together in the whole-farm view
farm.next_keep_b: Save plan keeps it in this browser (under Saved plans). Download plan gives you a PDF for your adviser. Save a copy to a file is a backup you can open on another computer.
farm.next_farm_in_one: This field is in your farm. Most farms have several: find the next one on the map. It opens right next to this field.
farm.next_farm_in_other: Your farm has {{count}} fields. Find the next one on the map: it opens right next to this field.
farm.next_farm_out: Most farms have several fields. Add this one to your farm, then find the next one on the map.
farm.next_whole_b: All your fields together: a typical year and a bad year, how the fields balance each other, and a plan that suits the whole farm.
farm.next_whole_empty: Add a field to your farm first.

sc.profit_help: How close each field's plan is to the best typical profit that field can make, acre-weighted. A plan that loses money in a typical year scores 3 at most.
sc.risk_help: From the whole farm's chance of a losing year: 10 = never, 1 = half the years or more. Fields that balance each other raise it.
sc.soil_help: Days with soil cover, water erosion, crop water use and soil carbon trend, against the field's other options (best = 10).
sc.f_profit_help: Profit: where this plan's typical profit sits between this field's worst and best options (best = 10). A plan that loses money in a typical year scores 3 at most.
sc.f_risk_help: Risk safety: from this field's chance of a losing year in the simulated seasons × price years: 10 = never, 1 = half the years or more.
sc.caveat: Scores compare plans on the same simulated weather and price years. They are not a forecast and not a guarantee: check locally before you decide.
sc.weights: Weighted for {{goal}}: profit {{p}} %, risk {{r}} %, soil & water {{s}} %. Change the goal under Find the best plan.
sc.boost_none: No single change raises the farm score by 0.1 or more. Try Find the best plan, or unlock fields.
sc.si_d1: Each plan's profit among the field's own options (simulated seasons × price years)
sc.si_d2: Chance of a losing year (whole farm, or the field)
sc.si_d3: Soil and water indicators from the field simulations
sc.si_r1: Scores compare plans on the same simulated years: not a forecast
sc.si_r_left_one: {{count}} field is left out until it has numbers
sc.si_r_left_other: {{count}} fields are left out until they have numbers
sc.si_r_soil: Soil & water not loaded for {{n}} field(s)
sc.si_raise: Enter your own yields, prices and costs on each field's money page
sc.adjust_help: Say how much each part matters to you. The farm score, every field's score and Raise your score update as you drag.
sc.weights_custom: Your own weights: profit {{p}} %, risk {{r}} %, soil & water {{s}} %.

board.help: Every field with its score. Click a field to see why, try other plans, or open it.

drawer.options_help: Each plan's field score, and what the farm score would be if you pick it. Your pick updates the whole dashboard.
drawer.how_h: How the score is worked out

farm.k_fields_waiting: {{n}} in the totals, {{w}} waiting for numbers
